interactions.summary: Jiang says the shocking part of the conflict will make sense only when read through eschatology and argues that destruction of Al-Aqsa would leave Gulf and Turkish regimes with almost no room to maneuver.
The host reinforces Jiang's point by noting Al-Aqsa's status in Islam and the unifying effect its destruction could have.
The host suggests regional elites may only be using rhetoric to suppress revolutionary pressure at home.
Jiang broadens the claim into a civilizational diagnosis: small groups of religious zealots have captured multiple elites and are pushing the world into cascading crises.
The host closes by summarizing a messy world-order transition and praising Jiang's work, while Jiang jokes that his longer lectures are not as easy to binge in one sitting.
The host asks whether Jiang wants to mention anything else before signing off.

claims.claim: Jiang says future shocks in the Middle East will remain incomprehensible unless people grasp the religious and eschatological structure of the conflict.
He argues Gulf-state and Turkish regimes are vulnerable because actions against Al-Aqsa would provoke millions of Muslims and sharply limit elite maneuverability.
Jiang says the contemporary world has been captured by small groups of fanatical religious zealots, including Christian Zionists and zealots across multiple traditions.
He says bureaucratic elites are stuck because they have no ideas and do not know how to respond to the crises now surrounding them.
Jiang predicts the next couple of years will bring a series of crises rather than a smooth transition to a new world order.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang insists that without the eschatological layer the whole conflict looks nonsensical, but with it the coming shock becomes legible.
signature_moments.source_phrase: unless you understand the religious eschatological elements to this conflict, then nothing makes sense
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This line crystallizes the interpretive key Jiang wants readers to carry away from the entire interview.

signature_moments.moment: The world is described as captured by small bands of fanatical religious zealots pushing multiple societies toward war and even apocalypse.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's been captured by small groups of fanatical religious zealots
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the interview's hottest and most memorable causal diagnoses.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The religious end-times logic Jiang says must be understood to make sense of elite behavior in the Middle East conflict.
Jiang's phrase for the near-future global condition produced by elite paralysis and zealot-driven escalation.

chronology_notes.note: This late-interview packet on 2025-09-18 compresses Jiang's final interpretive frame: eschatology explains the crisis and the next couple of years will be disorderly, not transitional in a calm sense.
